evidence: cgroup.memory.events.local.oom_kill increased by 1 across 1 adjacent sample pairs.
This records OOM victims in the counter's scope, not proof that the target was killed or that this cgroup's memory.max caused the kill.
findings.suggested_next_check: Correlate the target's exit status with kernel or provider evidence to establish the victim and the applicable memory limit.

evidence: cgroup.memory.stat.anon rose from 33554432 bytes (32.00 MiB) to 134217728 bytes (128.00 MiB) (increase 100663296 bytes (96.00 MiB)) over 15.000 seconds.
At least three sampled increases occurred; no single increase accounts for most of the net growth.
proc.status.RssAnon rose from 31457280 bytes (30.00 MiB) to 132120576 bytes (126.00 MiB) (increase 100663296 bytes (96.00 MiB)) over 15.000 seconds.
findings.suggested_next_check: Compare runtime heap metrics with process anonymous RSS in a controlled reproduction; anonymous memory alone cannot identify a leak or allocator.

evidence: A sample recorded cgroup.memory.current at 251658240 bytes (240.00 MiB) against cgroup.memory.max of 268435456 bytes (256.00 MiB) (93.8%).
The ratio uses physical cgroup memory only; swap is excluded from the denominator.
findings.suggested_next_check: Check the effective ancestor and VM limits as well as this cgroup's memory.max.

evidence: The recorder observed that the target disappeared.
A recording ending or a target disappearing does not establish its exit cause, even if a cgroup OOM counter also increased.
findings.suggested_next_check: Correlate the target's exit status with kernel or provider evidence.

collection_warnings.message: Ancestor cgroup limits were not evaluated; leaf memory utilization does not establish effective headroom.
A cgroup OOM counter does not identify the target as the victim or establish which memory limit caused the kill.
An incomplete final sample line was ignored; the tail of the incident may be missing.
Target process smaps_rollup metrics could not be read because permission was denied.
Sampling can miss peaks shorter than the sampling interval.
The target was observed in an exited or zombie state; process collection stopped for that observation.

limitations: Sampling can miss short peaks and cannot identify individual allocations or request counts.
Confidence is a deterministic evidence heuristic, not a calibrated probability.
Unchanged or unavailable OOM counters do not rule out a kill after the final sample.

Memory and process growth trends use only samples before the first observation marking the target absent; cgroup OOM-counter and utilization evidence can continue after disappearance. Memory released at target exit is not classified as workload recovery.
